extracted.intended_audience: research funders, higher-education policymakers, research administrators, and scholars of peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of the peer review process used to allocate research funding in higher education, relating reviewer ratings to characteristics of applicants and reviewers and offering recommendations to improve reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater reliability of peer review ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability of peer reviews was found to be disappointingly low (interrater agreement of .53 for researcher ratings based on an average of 4.3 external reviewers per proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report interrater agreement as a core quality metric for funding peer review. Low values (e.g., ~.53) indicate substantial measurement error and should motivate process changes (more reviews, different reviewer selection). Include the average number of reviewers per proposal when interpreting reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of researcher‑nominated reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researcher‑nominated external reviewers (those chosen by the authors of a research proposal) gave higher, less‑reliable ratings than panel‑nominated external reviewers chosen by the funding body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: do not use researcher‑nominated reviewers because they tend to inflate ratings and reduce reliability. Prefer panel‑nominated or centrally selected reviewers to reduce bias and increase consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviews per proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The study observed an average of 4.3 external reviewers per proposal and concluded that more reviews per proposal would improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase the number of independent external reviews per proposal to raise interrater reliability; explicitly consider tradeoffs of cost/time versus reliability. Track how reliability changes as reviews-per-proposal increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate reviews among a smaller number of highly selected reviewers in each subdiscipline
rubrics_metrics.description: A smaller number of more highly selected reviewers should perform most of the reviews within each subdiscipline, providing greater control over error associated with individual reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than many ad hoc reviewers, cultivate and assign a core, high‑quality reviewer pool within subdisciplines so errors attributable to individual reviewers are better controlled and reviewer quality is higher/consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and adjust for reviewer nationality/affiliation effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Australian external reviewers gave lower ratings than non‑Australian reviewers, particularly those from North America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess systematic differences in rating behavior by reviewer geography or institutional affiliation and consider statistical adjustments, reviewer calibration, or reviewer mix strategies to mitigate geographic/ cultural biases in ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit reviewer workload (number of proposals assessed per reviewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of proposals assessed by each external reviewer had small negative effects on ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading individual reviewers; cap the number of proposals assigned per reviewer to reduce fatigue effects and rating attenuation. Monitor rating patterns as reviewer workload changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for applicant characteristics and potential biases (seniority, gender, age, team size)
rubrics_metrics.description: The gender and age of a researcher and the number of researchers on a team did not affect funding probability in this study, but professors were more likely to be funded than non‑professors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate funding outcomes for evidence of bias by applicant characteristics (especially seniority). Where disparities exist (e.g., higher funding probability for professors), consider policy or review‑process changes to mitigate unfair advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical analysis to evaluate peer review process quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The article relates peer review ratings (2,989 proposals, 6,233 external reviewers) to characteristics of researchers and reviewers to assess reliability and sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly conduct large‑scale empirical analyses linking proposal ratings, reviewer attributes, and applicant attributes to detect reliability problems and systematic biases; use findings to justify operational changes (e.g., reviewer selection, review counts, workload limits).
